headline: Calibrated mechanistic models link promoter kinetics and stress-response dynamics
label: Mechanistic Models Of Regulatory Dynamics
summary: Calibrated, state-explicit models now tie regulatory and allosteric dynamics to measured dwell times and stress-response data.
synthesis: The dominant thread across these preprints is mechanistic, explicitly structured modeling of how regulatory systems produce dynamics and noise. The promoter study is the clearest case of explicit state accounting: discrete promoter states are treated as a continuous-time Markov chain, and the hybrid Markovian-ODE framework is parameterized from ChEC-seq dwell times, with the summary reporting agreement with SSA accuracy. The Integrated Stress Response model is calibrated to identify an eIF2 phosphorylation threshold, cascading ATF4, GADD34, CHOP and DR5 delays, and a biphasic amplitude limit. The allostery preprint is more abstract, using a spanning-tree framework with Burton-Pemantle path weighting to quantify communication and noise suppression in protein contact networks. What is new is pairing explicit transitions or pathway structure with quantities tied to data or defined graph statistics. Generalization beyond these three systems is not demonstrated by these items.
